newsitem.title: USA: Edison denied appeal on Pacific Pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Edison denied appeal on Pacific Pipeline.

text.p: A U.S. federal court has ruled that Edison International's Southern California Edison Co cannot appeal the U.S. Forest Service's approval of a crude oil pipeline project, the company that plans to operate the pipeline said on Monday.
The ruling by the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California was handed down a week ago, Pacific Pipeline System Inc, owned by Anschutz Co, said in a statement.
Edison argued that a competing pipeline proposal, which utilizes a segment of the utility's pipeline system, was a better project.

Pacific Pipeline filed a request to dismiss the appeal on December 20 after the city of Los Angeles said the process used by the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) to conduct environmental analyses was proper.
The 132-mile Pacific Pipeline, due to become operational by late 1997, would bring crude oil from offshore and San Joaquin Valley crude to Wilmington-area refineries.
